newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian banks rush to buy new 91-day T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Romanian banks rush to buy new 91-day T-bills.

text.p: Romanian banks rushed on Friday to buy fresh treasury bills against the background of a money market flooded with leu funds and increased one-week refinancing available from the central bank.
Seven banks bought 501 billion lei from the 620 billion worth of three-month treasury-bills offered by the Finance Ministry, central bank data showed.

Traders said the money market was saturated with leu funds which on short-term traded at about 43 percent. On Thursday the central bank raised its one-week offer to 1.180 trillion lei from last week's 1.045 trillion lei.
Friday's T-bills have an annual yield of 50.23 percent and mature on January 17, 1997.

Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA, Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare SA, Banca Comerciala Romana SA, Banc Post SA, Banca Agricola SA, Banca Ion Tiriac SA and Banca Romaneasca SA bought the Finance Ministry papers.
The Finance Ministry, keen to cover a rising 1996 state budget deficit, this month issued 1.0 trillion lei in 91-day bills to be placed in three public subscriptions.
At last week's session, six banks bought 380 billion lei worth of T-bills offering an annual yield of 51.35 percent. The remaining 119 billion lei will be on offer next Friday.
The January-August state budget showed a deficit of 1.9 trillion lei, while the forecast for the entire year is 4.27 trillion. ($=3,302 lei) -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
